issues.legal_issue: A criminal complaint and investigation alleging dishonest inducement to part with money cannot be quashed at the preliminary stage merely because the transaction also involves a civil dispute, where the allegations taken at face value prima facie disclose a cognizable offence.
material_facts: The complainant alleged that two persons represented that a plot of land could be sold to him and thereby induced him to enter into an agreement and pay money.
The complainant alleged that the persons had no valid title to the property and had conspired to induce payment without intending to complete the sale.
The complaint was referred for police investigation, and the High Court quashed the complaint proceedings and the resulting investigation before they could proceed.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the High Court's order quashing the proceedings was set aside, and the investigation was permitted to proceed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, a High Court ordinarily should not quash a criminal proceeding or FIR if the allegations, taken at face value and as a whole, disclose a cognizable offence. The power must be exercised sparingly; except in very exceptional circumstances, the court should not rely on defence documents or go beyond the allegations to decide the absence of mens rea or actus reus. A civil dispute does not by itself bar criminal proceedings. The Court relied on R. Kalyani v. Janak C. Mehta (2009) 1 SCC 516 and Mahesh Chaudhary v. State of Rajasthan (2009) 4 SCC 443, and distinguished Hridaya Ranjan Prasad Verma v. State of Bihar (2000) 4 SCC 168, Murari Lal Gupta v. Gopi Singh (2005) 13 SCC 699, and Ram Biraji Devi v. Umesh Kumar Singh (2006) 6 SCC 669 on their facts.

rule.if: quashing_challenge_during_investigation and dishonest_inducement_alleged and money_paid_in_reliance and allegations_taken_at_face_value_disclose_cognizable_offence

predicates.quashing_challenge_during_investigation: The matter is a challenge to the quashing of a criminal complaint or investigation before the investigation has run its course.
predicates.dishonest_inducement_alleged: The complainant alleges that a person dishonestly induced the complainant through representations made without an intention to perform the promised transaction.
predicates.money_paid_in_reliance: The complainant alleges that money was paid in reliance on the representations.
predicates.allegations_taken_at_face_value_disclose: Taking the complaint's allegations as true and reading them as a whole, they describe conduct that may amount to a cognizable offence.

issues.definition: When a challenge seeks to stop an investigation before it is complete and the complaint alleges dishonest inducement, payment in reliance, and facts that disclose a cognizable offence on their face, the investigation must be allowed to proceed.
